2	title: "Tools: animation"
3	description: Add actions to a clip from an agent, set what they animate to, zoom to a region, and move, re-curve or remove them.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	An [action](/motion/actions/) is a span on a clip over which its properties ease from what they are to an end state. These tools add one, say what it ends at, change its timing and take it away.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  tools={['add_action', 'add_zoom_action', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']}
12	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
13	  keys="⌥⌘K"
14	  where="Clip tab ▸ action lane"
15	/>
16	
17	The usual order is two calls. First, `add_action` with these arguments:
18	
19	```json
20	{ "clip": 12, "at": 600000, "duration": 1200000 }
21	```
22	
23	Then `set_action_end`, with the id it answered in `new_actions`:
24	
25	```json
26	{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": { "video": { "scale": 1.4 } } }
27	```
28	
29	Every time here is in ticks, 600,000 to the second, and is rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). An action's times are clip time, measured from the clip's own start, not the timeline's. `get_project` lists each clip's actions and their ids.
30	
31	For a speed ramp in one step, see `add_speed_ramp` on [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
32	
33	## `add_action`
34	
35	Adds an action to a clip. Its end state starts empty, so nothing changes until `set_action_end` fills it in. It mirrors **Clip ▸ Add Action** (<kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>) and the **+** button in the Clip tab's action lane. See [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/).
36	
37	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
38	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
39	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
40	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where the action starts, in clip time. |
41	| `duration` | integer | No | How long it runs. The default is 1 s (600,000). |
42	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
43	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
44	
45	**What it answers.** `ok`, `clip`, `new_actions` (a list holding the new action's id) and the `project` summary. A new action's curve is `linear`. Use `set_action` to change it.
46	
47	**When it refuses.**
48	
49	- It would overlap another action on the clip, or run past the clip's end. Both sentences give the times involved.
50	- A negative `at` or a `duration` that isn't positive is an error.
51	
52	## `add_zoom_action`
53	
54	Adds an action that zooms the picture to a rectangle, the screencast zoom, or back out to the clip's own framing. It mirrors the canvas's Z mode and the **Zoom to Region** and **Zoom Back** buttons in the Clip tab's action lane. See [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/).
55	
56	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
57	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
58	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
59	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where the zoom starts, in clip time. |
60	| `region` | object or null | Yes | The rectangle to zoom to, as `{x, y, width, height}`. `null` zooms back to the clip's own scale and position. |
61	| `duration` | integer | No | How long it runs. The default is 1 s (600,000). |
62	| `fit` | string | No | `fit`, the default, shows the whole region. `fill` covers the whole canvas, cropping whatever the region's shape doesn't match. |
63	| `curve` | string | No | How the zoom eases: `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` or `ease_in_out`. The default is `ease_in_out`. |
64	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
65	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
66	
67	```json
68	{ "clip": 12, "at": 0, "region": { "x": -320, "y": 180, "width": 640, "height": 360 } }
69	```
70	
71	`region` is in source pixels. `x` and `y` are its centre, measured from the centre of the clip's cropped picture, and `width` and `height` are its size. All four are required, and the key itself is required, so a forgotten rectangle can't turn into a zoom back.
72	
73	Over the action, the clip's `scale`, `x` and `y` ease to the values that bring the region to the canvas, measured through the clip's rotation. Rotation and crop are read as they are at `at`. The scale is held to the largest a clip can take, with the position worked out from that, so a region too small to fill the canvas still lands centred.
74	
75	**What it answers.** As `add_action`. The action is an ordinary one, so `set_action_end` can add to what it animates.
76	
77	**When it refuses.**
78	
79	- It would overlap another action or run past the clip's end, as `add_action`.
80	- A clip with no picture is an error: "clip 7 has no video properties".
81	- A `width` or `height` that isn't above 0, or a member the region doesn't have, is an error naming it.
82	
83	## `set_action`
84	
85	Moves an action, changes its length or changes its easing curve. It mirrors the selected action's start, length and curve controls in the Clip tab's action lane, and dragging a band. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
86	
87	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
88	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
89	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
90	| `action` | integer | Yes | The action's id. |
91	| `start` | integer | No | The new start, in clip time. |
92	| `duration` | integer | No | The new length. |
93	| `curve` | string | No | How the values ease: `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` or `ease_in_out`. |
94	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
95	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
96	
97	Give at least one of `start`, `duration` and `curve`. Any you leave out keep their value.
98	
99	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. When the action's end names a speed, captions on a Captions track wholly inside a clip with sound are re-timed in the same step: `captions_retimed` lists them, and `captions_removed` lists those whose speech it no longer plays. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
100	
101	**When it refuses.**
102	
103	- It would overlap another action on the clip.
104	- It would end past the clip's end and later than it ended before. An action a trim left past the clip's end can still be re-curved, moved earlier or shortened.
105	- On a speed action, it would make the clip read past the end of its media. The sentence names the latest clip end that fits.
106	- On a speed action of a linked clip, it would change the clip's speed: "clip 7 is linked to clip 8: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction".
107	- With none of the three arguments, the call answers "set_action needs start, duration or curve."
108	
109	## `set_action_end`
110	
111	Sets what an action animates to. It mirrors every inspector field written while an action is selected. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) and [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).
112	
113	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
114	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
115	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
116	| `action` | integer | Yes | The action's id. |
117	| `patch` | object | Yes | The end state, with `video`, `audio`, `text` and `graphic` groups and a top-level `speed`. |
118	| `off` | array of strings | No | `"group.key"` paths to switch off at the end. See [Switching off at an end](#switching-off-at-an-end). |
119	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
120	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
121	
122	```json
123	{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": { "video": { "opacity": 0 }, "audio": { "volume": 0.2 } } }
124	```
125	
126	The patch merges into the end state key by key, at every depth, so a one-key `shadow` keeps the rest of it. A key set to `null` is removed from the end state, so that property stops being animated, and a group set to `null` removes the whole group.
127	
128	The `video`, `audio` and `text` groups take the same keys as [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/), [`set_audio`](/mcp/tools-set-audio/) and [`set_text`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/). A colour is four numbers here too, and it ramps in OKLab with straight alpha. So do the chroma key's three numbers.
129	
130	A bad key or value is refused by its path with the group in it, such as `video.filters[1].kind`. Values aren't range-checked, though: an animation can aim past what a stored property could hold.
131	
132	**Sound.** Every key the sound's effects read animates: `pan`, `mono`, `channels`, `eq`, `hum`, `noise_reduction`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser`, `compressor`, `limiter` and `isolation`, beside `volume` and the fades.
133	
134	- Numbers ramp.
135	- A switch changes when the action ends: a group or an EQ slot turned on, `mono`, `channels`, an EQ slope, hum's frequency and harmonics, and the leveller's response.
136	- `isolation` ramps from 0 on a clip with none.
137	- `duck`, `keep_pitch`, the fade shapes and `voice` are stored but never animate.
138	
139	See [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/).
140	
141	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. With `speed` in the patch it can add the keys listed under [Speed in an action](#speed-in-an-action).
142	
143	**When it refuses.** These keys are errors, a `null` included:
144	
145	| Key | Why, and what to do instead |
146	| --- | --- |
147	| `video.motion` | It's a preset tied to the clip's two ends. Set it with `set_video`. |
148	| `video.hide_silent` | It isn't an animation target. Set it with `set_video`. |
149	| `text.words` | Word times belong to speech. Set them with `set_text`. |
150	| `video.cutout.subject`, `video.cutout.quality` | They're the clip's own. Set them with `set_video`. A cutout's `edge`, `feather` and `background` do animate. |
151	| Any `shape` key | Shapes can't be animated, so `shape` isn't a group here. |
152	
153	### Animating graphic props
154	
155	A graphic clip's props are a fourth group: `graphic: {props: {<key>: <value>}}`, keyed by what its module declares. It mirrors the Graphic sub-tab's **Properties** with an action selected. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
156	
157	```json
158	{ "clip": 18, "action": 44, "patch": { "graphic": { "props": { "accent": "#ff5500", "count": 96 } } } }
159	```
160	
161	- A value is checked as `set_graphic` checks it, minimum and maximum included, against the module as the project's graphics folder holds it now.
162	- A number ramps along the curve and arrives with decimals, so 64 to 129 is 96.5 halfway. A module that needs a whole number rounds it.
163	- A colour blends in OKLab, with straight alpha.
164	- A string, a boolean and an enum switch to the end's value when the action ends.
165	- An image prop switches when the action ends. `""` names no image there.
166	- A prop the clip holds no value for starts from the module's current default, written into the clip in the same undo step.
167	- `graphic.props.<key>: null` removes that prop from the end, and `graphic: null` removes the whole group.
168	
169	`get_project` shows `kinds` beside `props`. Frame Job writes that and ignores any you send, so an end you read back can be sent again.
170	
171	**When it refuses.**
172	
173	- A prop its module marks `animate: false` is refused. Set it with `set_graphic`.
174	- `name`, `width`, `height`, `in` and `length` are refused: an action animates `graphic.props` only.
175	- While the module is missing or doesn't compile, a value is refused, and `get_graphic` says why. A `null` still removes.
176	- On a clip that isn't a graphic: "clip 7 is not a graphic clip".
177	
178	### Speed in an action
179	
180	`speed`, a number beside the groups, is a media clip's rate. The clip ramps from the rate in force to it along the curve and holds it after, and it keeps its start and length, playing more or less source. It mirrors the Speed section's **Rate** with an action selected. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/).
181	
182	```json
183	{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": { "speed": 3 } }
184	```
185	
186	The rate is clamped to ×0.1–×1000, and `speed: null` removes it.
187	
188	Above ×12 the clip's audio is left out, and the answer carries `audio_left_out` (the clip ids) and `audio_note`. Captions on a Captions track wholly inside a clip with sound are re-timed in the same step: `captions_retimed` lists them, and `captions_removed` lists those whose speech it no longer plays.
189	
190	**When it refuses.**
191	
192	- An end rate that would read past the end of the clip's media. The sentence names the largest end rate that fits.
193	- `speed: null` when the clip would then read past the end of its media. The sentence names the latest clip end that fits.
194	- A value that isn't a number or `null`, or a clip that isn't a media clip.
195	- A rate on a linked clip: "clip 7 is linked to clip 8: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction".
196	
197	### Switching off at an end
198	
199	`off` turns an optional property off at the end of the action. The path is stored as a `null` in the end state, where a `null` in `patch` removes the key instead. So `off` means "this shadow goes away by the end", and a `null` in `patch` means "stop animating the shadow".
200	
201	```json
202	{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": {}, "off": ["video.shadow", "audio.eq.band_2"] }
203	```
204	
205	- A path is `"group.key"`, with a group of `video`, `audio` or `text` and one of its top-level keys, such as `video.shadow`, `text.width` or `audio.limiter`.
206	- One deeper path exists: `audio.eq.<slot>` switches that EQ slot off. The slots are `high_pass`, `low_shelf`, `band_1`, `band_2`, `band_3`, `high_shelf` and `low_pass`.
207	- Only optional keys can go off. A required key such as `video.opacity` is refused.
208	- A path can't also be named in `patch`.
209	- `graphic` paths are refused: name the value a prop ends at in `patch`.
210	- `video.cutout` is refused: `set_video` with `{cutout: null}` removes a cutout.
211	- `video.motion`, `video.hide_silent` and `text.words` are refused here too.
212	
213	## `remove_action`
214	
215	Removes an action. The clip keeps its base properties. It mirrors the action lane's trash button and <kbd>⌫</kbd> with an action selected. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
216	
217	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
218	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
219	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
220	| `action` | integer | Yes | The action's id. |
221	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
222	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
223	
224	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. When the action named a speed, captions are re-timed in the same step, with `captions_retimed` and `captions_removed` as for `set_action`.
225	
226	**When it refuses.**
227	
228	- Removing a speed action when the clip would then read past the end of its media. The sentence names the latest clip end that fits.
229	- Removing a speed action from a linked clip: "clip 7 is linked to clip 8: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction".
230	- An action id the clip doesn't have is an error.
231	
232	## Related
233

235	- [Patches](/mcp/patches/)
236	- [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/)
237	- [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/)
238	- [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/)

2	title: "Tools: transitions"
3	description: Make a transition at a hard cut from an agent, change its kind, length and easing, crossfade the sound, or remove it.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A [transition](/motion/transitions/) plays across the overlap between a clip and the clip before it on the same track, and it belongs to the later clip. Its length is that overlap. These tools make the overlap, choose the transition, and set how it eases and sounds.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  tools={['add_transition', 'set_transition', 'set_transition_duration', 'set_transition_style']}
12	  menu="Clip ▸ Transition ▸"
13	  where="Clip tab ▸ Transition section"
14	/>
15	
16	Start with `add_transition` at a hard cut. Use `set_transition` and `set_transition_duration` on clips that already overlap.
17	
18	Every time here is in ticks, 600,000 to the second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
19	
20	The kinds are `cross_dissolve`, `fade_black`, `fade_white`, `push_left`, `push_right`, `push_up`, `push_down`, `wipe`, `slide`, `zoom`, `wipe_left`, `wipe_up` and `wipe_down`. See [Transition styles](/motion/transition-styles/).
21	
22	An adjustment clip can't take a transition or overlap another clip, so these tools refuse one, and `set_transition` with `kind: null` is the only call that goes through. Fade it with opacity instead. See [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/).
23	
24	## `add_transition`
25	
26	Makes an overlap at the hard cut before a clip and puts a transition on it. It mirrors **Clip ▸ Transition ▸** on a clip that butts up against the one before it. See [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/).
27	
28	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
29	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
30	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The incoming clip's id. |
31	| `duration` | integer | Yes | The overlap you want. It can land shorter, but it's never refused for being too long. |
32	| `kind` | string | No | The transition. Left out, it's the clip's stored kind, else `cross_dissolve`. It can't be `null`: `set_transition` clears one. |
33	| `align` | string | No | Which side the overlap comes out of: `center`, the default, `before` or `after`. Ignored with `ripple`. |
34	| `ripple` | boolean or string | No | `true` makes the overlap by sliding the incoming clip and everything after it left, for two clips with no footage beyond the cut. The default is `false`. |
35	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
36	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
37	
38	```json
39	{ "clip": 15, "duration": 600000, "kind": "fade_black" }
40	```
41	
42	**How the overlap is made.** It's built from material the two clips already have: the source before the incoming clip's in point, and after the outgoing clip's out point. Nothing else on the timeline moves, and the pair's outer edges stay where they were.
43	
44	| `align` | Where the overlap comes from |
45	| --- | --- |
46	| `center` | Half from each side. An odd frame goes to the incoming clip, and a side with nothing to give passes its share to the other. |
47	| `before` | All from the incoming clip's head. |
48	| `after` | All from the outgoing clip's tail. |
49	
50	`duration` snaps down to whole frames. It's then held to each side's spare material, to the neighbours on the track and to the limit on how far two clips can overlap, so a request too long for the media lands shorter. A nest clip has no spare head, and its tail ends at the nest's own length.
51	
52	A stored transition keeps its curve and crossfade. A new one eases at both ends and crossfades its sound. The incoming clip's actions move with its new first frame, so a zoom stays on the source frame it was drawn over.
53	
54	**With `ripple: true`.** This is the sheet's **Shift Clips Left** button, for when neither clip has footage beyond the cut. No material is read and `align` is ignored. The incoming clip and every clip at or after the cut, on every unlocked track, slide left by `duration`, so the timeline gets that much shorter and no clip's source window changes.
55	
56	- The shift is capped at half the shorter of the two clips.
57	- It's also limited to the largest whole-frame shift that leaves every moved track within the overlap limit.
58	- A clip on another track pushed into its neighbour gets a `cross_dissolve`.
59	- Markers don't move.
60	
61	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary.
62	
63	**When it refuses.**
64	
65	- A `duration` that isn't positive is an error.
66	- A clip not at a hard cut is an error naming which of three: it's the first clip on its track, there's a gap before it, or it already overlaps a clip. For that last one, use `set_transition` or `set_transition_duration`.
67	- A `duration` under one frame is refused, naming the shortest that passes.
68	- A cut with no room: the request clamps to nothing against the two clips' spare material, their neighbours and the overlap limit. The sentence suggests `ripple: true`.
69	- A track already outside the overlap limit is refused by that rule before anything is fitted.
70	- With `ripple`: an incoming clip on a locked track, or clips with no room to overlap by shifting.
71	
72	## `set_transition`
73	
74	Sets the transition into a clip, or removes it. It mirrors the **Kind** pop-up in the Clip tab's **Transition** section. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
75	
76	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
77	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
78	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
79	| `kind` | string or null | Yes | The transition, or `null` to remove it. |
80	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
81	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
82	
83	The transition's length is the clip's overlap with the one before it, so a clip with no overlap ignores it until it has one. Make an overlap with `move_clip` or `set_transition_duration`. Changing the kind keeps the transition's curve and crossfade. A new one eases at both ends and crossfades its sound.
84	
85	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary.
86	
87	**When it refuses.** A missing `kind`, or a value that isn't one of the thirteen or `null`, is an error listing them.
88	
89	## `set_transition_duration`
90	
91	Makes a transition last `duration` by moving the clip, so its overlap with the clip before it equals that. It mirrors the **Duration** field in the Clip tab's **Transition** section. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
92	
93	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
94	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
95	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
96	| `duration` | integer | Yes | The overlap length, rounded to the frame grid. |
97	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
98	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
99	
100	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary.
101	
102	**When it refuses.**
103	
104	- On a track's first clip, which has nothing to overlap.
105	- Past half the shorter clip, snapped down. The sentence names that limit in ticks.
106	- A `duration` that isn't positive is an error. To clear a transition, use `set_transition` with `kind: null`.
107	
108	## `set_transition_style`
109	
110	Sets how a transition is eased, whether it crossfades the two clips' sound, and the crossfade's shape. It mirrors the **Curve** pop-up, the **Crossfade Audio** checkbox and the **Crossfade Shape** pop-up in the Clip tab's **Transition** section. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
111	
112	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
113	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
114	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
115	| `curve` | string | No | How the transition's progress is eased: `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` or `ease_in_out`. |
116	| `audio` | boolean or string | No | Crossfades the two clips' sound across the overlap. |
117	| `audio_shape` | string | No | The crossfade's curve. See the table below. |
118	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
119	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
120	
121	`audio` and `ripple` take `true` or `false`, or those words or `"1"` and `"0"` as strings.
122	
123	| `audio_shape` | The curve, over the eased progress p |
124	| --- | --- |
125	| `plus_3db` | The default, constant power: sine in, cosine out. It holds the level across two unrelated takes, where a straight-line pair dips 3 dB. |
126	| `linear` | p in, 1 − p out. |
127	| `s_curve` | A slow start. |
128	| `minus_3db` | A slow start. |
129	
130	The outgoing clip takes the shape of 1 − p.
131	
132	A key you leave out keeps what's there, so changing the curve never touches the crossfade, and the other way round.
133	
134	The tool writes onto any clip, with or without an overlap. A stored transition on a clip with no overlap isn't drawn until there is one. A clip with no transition at all gets a `cross_dissolve` with the style applied.
135	
136	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary.
137	
138	**When it refuses.** With none of the three keys, the call is an error naming them.
139

143	- [Transition styles](/motion/transition-styles/)

transition_search.rs transition.rs video_gate.rs webm_ebml_block.rs webm_ebml.rs webm_layout.rs webm_writer.rs # core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_media.rs` — the media types (`Media`, `MediaOriginal`, `MediaKind`,
  spec §5.2's `media[]`), moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map
  "creator-jobs" CJ0b's toll T2) and re-exported by it, so every
  `crate::model::Media*` path holds; a media record's new keys land here.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s
  `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence (`audio.eq.<slot>.frequency
  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not
  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stage is Swift's.
- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /
  `check_de_esser` / `check_leveller`, run by
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence
  (`audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21`; times through
  `props_check.rs`'s `ticks_in_range`), `check_compressor` /
  `check_limiter` (under a prefix: `audio.` for the clip's, run by
  `check_audio`, and the track's own key for `track_dynamics.rs`, spec §11
  AU-150), and `clamp_gate` / `clamp_de_esser` / `clamp_leveller`
  (each field to its range, NaN to its default), run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stages are Swift's.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s

1	---
2	title: "Tools: text, shapes and clip names"
3	description: Restyle text and caption words, change a shape's geometry and paint, name and label clips, and put a title behind a person, from an agent.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These tools change what a text or shape clip holds, what a clip is called, and how a title sits behind a person. Where a text or shape clip sits on the canvas is a separate matter: its position and scale are [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/)'s.
9	
10	<AtAGlance tools={['set_text', 'set_shape', 'set_clip', 'text_behind_subject']} />
11	
12	`set_text`, `set_shape` and `set_clip` each take a patch that merges into the clip: a key you leave out keeps its value, and a key set to `null` clears it where the key can be empty. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/). A colour is four numbers, `[r, g, b, a]`, each 0 to 1. Three numbers are refused, and so is a value outside the range. Each edit is one undo step however many clips it names, and answers `ok` and the `project` summary. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
13	
14	## `set_text`
15	
16	Changes a text clip's words and typography. It mirrors the Clip tab's Text sub-tab. See [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/).
17	
18	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
19	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
20	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The text clips to change, at least one. `get_project` lists their ids. |
21	| `patch` | object | Yes | The text properties to change. The table below lists its keys. |
22	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
23	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
24	
25	| Patch key | What it does | Values |
26	| --- | --- | --- |
27	| `content` | The words. | A string |
28	| `font` | The font, by its PostScript name. | A string |
29	| `size` | The size, in pixels. | Above 0 |
30	| `color` | The text's colour. | Four numbers |
31	| `align` | Horizontal alignment. | `left`, `center`, `right` |
32	| `valign` | Vertical alignment. | `top`, `middle`, `bottom` |
33	| `line_spacing` | The space between lines. | Above 0 |
34	| `tracking` | The space between letters. | Any number |
35	| `outline` | An outline around the letters. | `null`, or `{width, color}` |
36	| `backdrop` | A coloured box behind the text. | `null`, or `{color, padding, radius}` |
37	| `width` | The width to wrap at, in pixels. `null` restores auto-sizing. | `null`, or above 0 |
38	| `animation` | How the words arrive and leave. | `null`, or `{kind, in, out}` |
39	| `case` | `upper` sets the text in capitals before layout, and never changes the word count. | `as_written`, `upper` |
40	| `words` | When each word of a caption page is said. See [Word timings and word style](#word-timings-and-word-style). | A list, or `[]` |
41	| `word_style` | How the word being said is drawn. See [Word timings and word style](#word-timings-and-word-style). | `null`, or an object |
42	
43	```json
44	{ "clips": [21], "patch": { "content": "Chapter two", "size": 96, "outline": { "width": 3 } } }
45	```
46	
47	**Outline and backdrop.** `outline` starts from a width of 2 in black, and `backdrop` from black at 0.6 alpha with padding 12 and radius 8. Width, padding and radius are 0 or more. See [Text outline and backdrop](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/).
48	
49	**Animation.** `kind` is `typewriter`, `word_fade` or `line_rise`. `in` and `out` are durations in ticks, measured from the clip's first and last frame, and both snap to the frame grid. Either can be 0 for no ramp at that end, and `in` plus `out` longer than the clip shows a partial reveal. It merges, `{animation: null}` clears it, and it starts from a one-second `typewriter` with no `out`. A negative duration is an error. See [Text reveals](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/).
50	
51	**When it refuses.** A key the patch doesn't know, a value outside its range, or a clip that isn't a text clip ("clip 7 has no text properties") is an error naming what's wrong.
52	
53	## Word timings and word style
54	
55	A caption page is a text clip with a time on each word. `set_text` edits these like any other text key. See [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/) and [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/).
56	
57	### Word timings
58	
59	`words` is one `{start, end}` per whitespace-separated word of `content`, in ticks from the clip's start, or `[]` for an untimed page.
60	
61	- When the list isn't empty, it must hold exactly one timing for each word. If not, the call answers "this text is timed word by word: 5 timings for 6 words".
62	- A change to `content` that alters the word count must send `words: []` in the same patch.
63	- A word's `end` can't come before its `start`, and each `start` can't come before the one before it. Two words can start together.
64	- A negative `start` is allowed. It means the word was already being said when the clip began.
65	- The times snap to the frame grid, so two words can land on one frame.
66	
67	`words` can't be animated: `set_action_end` refuses it.
68	
69	### Word style
70	
71	`word_style` is `null` or an object. It replaces `animation` on the page.
72	
73	| Key | What it does | Values | Default |
74	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
75	| `mode` | `highlight` draws the whole page and picks out the active word. `build` makes words appear as they're said. | `highlight`, `build` | `highlight` |
76	| `active_color` | The active word's colour. | Four numbers | The text's colour |
77	| `active_scale` | Where the active word's pop settles. 1 is no pop. | 1 to 1.5 | 1 |
78	| `active_pill` | A rounded plate behind the active word. | `null`, or `{color, padding, radius, glide}` | No plate |
79	| `spoken_color` | The colour of words already said. | Four numbers | The text's colour |
80	| `upcoming_color` | The colour of words not yet said, in `highlight` mode. | Four numbers | The text's colour |
81	| `active_fill` | Fills the active word left to right as it's said. | `true`, `false` | `false` |
82	| `pause_dim` | How far the words and pill fade in a pause. | 0 to 1 | 0 |
83	
84	**The pill.** Its `padding` and `radius` are fractions of the text's `size`, starting from 0.2 and 0.25, and its `color` starts as purple. `glide` set to `true` slides the pill from the word before to the active one over 0.2 s, or sooner when the next word starts sooner, instead of jumping.
85	
86	**The fill.** `active_fill` runs from the word's start to its end, taking 0.6 s at most. The part already said draws in `active_color` and the rest in `upcoming_color`, or isn't drawn yet in `build` mode. In `highlight` mode it shows only where those two colours differ.
87	
88	**The pause dim.** `pause_dim` fades the words and the pill to 1 minus `pause_dim` of their opacity, over 0.1 s each way, in a pause of 0.25 s or more. A pause runs from one word's end to the next one's start, before a late first word, and after the last word until the clip ends.
89	
90	```json
91	{ "word_style": { "active_pill": { "glide": true }, "pause_dim": 0.5 } }
92	```
93	
94	## `set_shape`
95	
96	Changes a shape clip's geometry and paint. It mirrors the Clip tab's Shape sub-tab. See [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/).
97	
98	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
99	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
100	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The shape clips to change, at least one. `get_project` lists their ids. |
101	| `patch` | object | Yes | The shape properties to change. The table below lists its keys. |
102	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
103	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
104	
105	| Patch key | What it does | Values |
106	| --- | --- | --- |
107	| `kind` | The shape. Changing it changes only the kind. | `rectangle`, `ellipse`, `line`, `arrow` |
108	| `width`, `height` | The box, in source pixels. | Above 0 |
109	| `stroke` | The outline. `null` removes it. | `null`, or `{width, color}` |
110	| `fill` | The flat fill. `null` removes it. | `null`, or a colour |
111	| `radius` | A rectangle's corners. | 0 or more |
112	| `arrow_start`, `arrow_end` | Whether a line or arrow has a head at that end. | `true`, `false` |
113	| `from`, `to` | A line's or arrow's ends, as unit coordinates in its box. | Two numbers each, such as `[0, 1]` and `[1, 0]` |
114	| `gradient` | A gradient fill. | `null`, or `{kind, stops, angle}` |
115	
116	```json
117	{ "clips": [30], "patch": { "fill": [0.1, 0.2, 0.9, 1], "stroke": null, "radius": 24 } }
118	```
119	
120	Because changing `kind` changes only the kind, an arrow made this way keeps whatever `arrow_end` it had, unlike one created by `add_shape_clip`. See [Lines and arrows](/text-and-shapes/lines-and-arrows/).
121	
122	**Gradient.** A gradient takes precedence over `fill` while it's set and leaves `fill` in place, so `{gradient: null}` brings the flat colour back. `{gradient: {}}` starts a black-to-white ramp running left to right. See [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/).
123	
124	| Key | What it does | Values |
125	| --- | --- | --- |
126	| `kind` | The ramp's form. A radial gradient is an ellipse inscribed in the box. | `linear`, `radial` |
127	| `stops` | 2 to 8 `{at, color}` objects, `at` being 0 to 1 along the ramp. They needn't be sorted. Sending `stops` replaces them all. | A list |
128	| `angle` | Degrees from the right, turning counter-clockwise. It means nothing for `radial`. | Any number |
129	
130	A `line` or `arrow` has no area and ignores the gradient.
131	
132	**When it refuses.** A key the patch doesn't know, a value outside its range, or a clip that isn't a shape clip ("clip 7 has no shape properties") is an error naming what's wrong. Shapes can't be animated: an action's end has no shape group.
133	
134	## `set_clip`
135	
136	Sets a clip's name and colour label. It mirrors the timeline's inline rename, the Clip tab's name field, **Clip ▸ Rename…** (<kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd>) and **Clip ▸ Label ▸**. See [Clip names and labels](/timeline/names-and-labels/).
137	
138	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
139	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
140	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to change, at least one. `get_project` lists their ids. |
141	| `patch` | object | Yes | `name`, `label` or both. A key left out keeps its value, and `null` clears it. |
142	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
143	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
144	
145	```json
146	{ "clips": [12], "patch": { "name": "Intro", "label": "green" } }
147	```
148	
149	**Names.** Names are trimmed, and an empty or blank name clears the name, as `null` does. A clip with no name of its own shows what it holds: the nest, the media file, or its kind.
150	
151	**Labels.** The six labels are `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `blue` and `purple`, drawn as a dot on the clip. The label is stored as given, so keep to these names. Any other name draws in the neutral text colour.
152	
153	A split, duplicate, detach or paste carries the name and label along. `paste_attributes` never does.
154	
155	**When it refuses.** A key other than `name` or `label`, or a value that's neither a string nor `null`, is an error.
156	
157	## `text_behind_subject`
158	
159	Puts a title behind the person in a clip of a video file or a picture, in one undo step. It mirrors **Insert ▸ Text Behind Subject**. See [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/).
160	
161	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
162	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
163	| `clip` | integer | No | The clip to put the title behind. Left out, it's picked at `at`. |
164	| `content` | string | No | The title's text. Left out, it's the Title preset's. |
165	| `at` | integer | No | Where the title starts, in ticks, snapped to the frame grid. Left out, it's the playhead. |
166	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
167	
168	The step does four things:
169	
170	- It adds a track named "Behind Subject" directly above the clip's track, and above any matte tracks in front of it.
171	- It adds a text clip with the Title preset at `at`, for 4 s or the rest of the clip if that's shorter.
172	- It sets `behind_subject` on the title.
173	- If the clip has no cutout yet, it sets `{cutout: {background: keep}}` on it, so the camera stays whole and the person still hides the title.
174	
175	The person's masks are made on your Mac, with no key. `analyze_cutout` says where they stand. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).
176	
177	**Which clip it picks.** Without `clip`, it looks at the clips of a video file or a picture playing at `at`, on a shown track that isn't a matte track. It takes the front-most selected one, else the front-most with a cutout, else the front-most. The selection is left as it was.
178	
179	**What it answers.**
180	
181	| Key | What it is |
182	| --- | --- |
183	| `ok` | `true`. |
184	| `clip` | The clip the title is behind. |
185	| `track` | The new track's id. |
186	| `text` | The title's clip id. |
187	| `duration` | The title's length, in ticks. |
188	| `cutout_added` | Whether the clip was given a cutout. |
189	| `project` | The project summary. |
190	
191	**When it refuses.** Nothing is done when:
192	
193	- A nest is open. It works on the top-level timeline only, so call `set_scope` with no nest first.
194	- `content` is empty.
195	- No clip of a video file or a picture plays at `at` on a shown track that isn't a matte track.
196	- The named clip isn't a clip of a video file or a picture, on a shown track that isn't a matte track.
197	- The named clip doesn't play at `at`.
198	
199	To put any other drawing clip behind the subject by hand, use `set_video` with [`behind_subject`](/mcp/tools-set-video/). An adjustment or nest clip can't take it.
200	
201	## Related
202	
203	- [Patches](/mcp/patches/)
204	- [Tools: picture and grade (set_video)](/mcp/tools-set-video/)
205	- [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/)
206	- [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/)
207

1	---
2	title: "Tools: animation"
3	description: Add actions to a clip from an agent, set what they animate to, zoom to a region, and move, re-curve or remove them.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	An [action](/motion/actions/) is a span on a clip over which its properties ease from what they are to an end state. These tools add one, say what it ends at, change its timing and take it away.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  tools={['add_action', 'add_zoom_action', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']}
12	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
13	  keys="⌥⌘K"
14	  where="Clip tab ▸ action lane"
15	/>
16	
17	The usual order is two calls. First, `add_action` with these arguments:
18	
19	```json
20	{ "clip": 12, "at": 600000, "duration": 1200000 }
21	```
22	
23	Then `set_action_end`, with the id it answered in `new_actions`:
24	
25	```json
26	{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": { "video": { "scale": 1.4 } } }
27	```
28	
29	Every time here is in ticks, 600,000 to the second, and is rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). An action's times are clip time, measured from the clip's own start, not the timeline's. `get_project` lists each clip's actions and their ids.
30	
31	For a speed ramp in one step, see `add_speed_ramp` on [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
32	
33	## `add_action`
34	
35	Adds an action to a clip. Its end state starts empty, so nothing changes until `set_action_end` fills it in. It mirrors **Clip ▸ Add Action** (<kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>) and the **+** button in the Clip tab's action lane. See [Add an action](/motion/add-an-action/).
36	
37	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
38	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
39	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
40	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where the action starts, in clip time. |
41	| `duration` | integer | No | How long it runs. The default is 1 s (600,000). |
42	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
43	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
44	
45	**What it answers.** `ok`, `clip`, `new_actions` (a list holding the new action's id) and the `project` summary. A new action's curve is `linear`. Use `set_action` to change it.
46	
47	**When it refuses.**
48	
49	- It would overlap another action on the clip, or run past the clip's end. Both sentences give the times involved.
50	- A negative `at` or a `duration` that isn't positive is an error.
51	
52	## `add_zoom_action`
53	
54	Adds an action that zooms the picture to a rectangle, the screencast zoom, or back out to the clip's own framing. It mirrors the canvas's Z mode and the **Zoom to Region** and **Zoom Back** buttons in the Clip tab's action lane. See [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/).
55	
56	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
57	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
58	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
59	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where the zoom starts, in clip time. |
60	| `region` | object or null | Yes | The rectangle to zoom to, as `{x, y, width, height}`. `null` zooms back to the clip's own scale and position. |
61	| `duration` | integer | No | How long it runs. The default is 1 s (600,000). |
62	| `fit` | string | No | `fit`, the default, shows the whole region. `fill` covers the whole canvas, cropping whatever the region's shape doesn't match. |
63	| `curve` | string | No | How the zoom eases: `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` or `ease_in_out`. The default is `ease_in_out`. |
64	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
65	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
66	
67	```json
68	{ "clip": 12, "at": 0, "region": { "x": -320, "y": 180, "width": 640, "height": 360 } }
69	```
70	
71	`region` is in source pixels. `x` and `y` are its centre, measured from the centre of the clip's cropped picture, and `width` and `height` are its size. All four are required, and the key itself is required, so a forgotten rectangle can't turn into a zoom back.
72	
73	Over the action, the clip's `scale`, `x` and `y` ease to the values that bring the region to the canvas, measured through the clip's rotation. Rotation and crop are read as they are at `at`. The scale is held to the largest a clip can take, with the position worked out from that, so a region too small to fill the canvas still lands centred.
74	
75	**What it answers.** As `add_action`. The action is an ordinary one, so `set_action_end` can add to what it animates.
76	
77	**When it refuses.**
78	
79	- It would overlap another action or run past the clip's end, as `add_action`.
80	- A clip with no picture is an error: "clip 7 has no video properties".
81	- A `width` or `height` that isn't above 0, or a member the region doesn't have, is an error naming it.
82	
83	## `set_action`
84	
85	Moves an action, changes its length or changes its easing curve. It mirrors the selected action's start, length and curve controls in the Clip tab's action lane, and dragging a band. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
86	
87	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
88	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
89	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
90	| `action` | integer | Yes | The action's id. |
91	| `start` | integer | No | The new start, in clip time. |
92	| `duration` | integer | No | The new length. |
93	| `curve` | string | No | How the values ease: `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` or `ease_in_out`. |
94	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
95	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
96	
97	Give at least one of `start`, `duration` and `curve`. Any you leave out keep their value.
98	
99	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. When the action's end names a speed, captions on a Captions track wholly inside a clip with sound are re-timed in the same step: `captions_retimed` lists them, and `captions_removed` lists those whose speech it no longer plays. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
100	
101	**When it refuses.**
102	
103	- It would overlap another action on the clip.
104	- It would end past the clip's end and later than it ended before. An action a trim left past the clip's end can still be re-curved, moved earlier or shortened.
105	- On a speed action, it would make the clip read past the end of its media. The sentence names the latest clip end that fits.
106	- On a speed action of a linked clip, it would change the clip's speed: "clip 7 is linked to clip 8: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction".
107	- With none of the three arguments, the call answers "set_action needs start, duration or curve."
108	
109	## `set_action_end`
110	
111	Sets what an action animates to. It mirrors every inspector field written while an action is selected. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) and [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).
112	
113	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
114	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
115	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
116	| `action` | integer | Yes | The action's id. |
117	| `patch` | object | Yes | The end state, with `video`, `audio`, `text` and `graphic` groups and a top-level `speed`. |
118	| `off` | array of strings | No | `"group.key"` paths to switch off at the end. See [Switching off at an end](#switching-off-at-an-end). |
119	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
120	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
121	
122	```json
123	{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": { "video": { "opacity": 0 }, "audio": { "volume": 0.2 } } }
124	```
125	
126	The patch merges into the end state key by key, at every depth, so a one-key `shadow` keeps the rest of it. A key set to `null` is removed from the end state, so that property stops being animated, and a group set to `null` removes the whole group.
127	
128	The `video`, `audio` and `text` groups take the same keys as [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/), [`set_audio`](/mcp/tools-set-audio/) and [`set_text`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/). A colour is four numbers here too, and it ramps in OKLab with straight alpha. So do the chroma key's three numbers.
129	
130	A bad key or value is refused by its path with the group in it, such as `video.filters[1].kind`. Values aren't range-checked, though: an animation can aim past what a stored property could hold.
131	
132	**Sound.** Every key the sound's effects read animates: `pan`, `mono`, `channels`, `eq`, `hum`, `noise_reduction`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser`, `compressor`, `limiter` and `isolation`, beside `volume` and the fades.
133	
134	- Numbers ramp.
135	- A switch changes when the action ends: a group or an EQ slot turned on, `mono`, `channels`, an EQ slope, hum's frequency and harmonics, and the leveller's response.
136	- `isolation` ramps from 0 on a clip with none.
137	- `duck`, `keep_pitch`, the fade shapes and `voice` are stored but never animate.
138	
139	See [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/).
140	
141	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. With `speed` in the patch it can add the keys listed under [Speed in an action](#speed-in-an-action).
142	
143	**When it refuses.** These keys are errors, a `null` included:
144	
145	| Key | Why, and what to do instead |
146	| --- | --- |
147	| `video.motion` | It's a preset tied to the clip's two ends. Set it with `set_video`. |
148	| `video.hide_silent` | It isn't an animation target. Set it with `set_video`. |
149	| `text.words` | Word times belong to speech. Set them with `set_text`. |
150	| `video.cutout.subject`, `video.cutout.quality` | They're the clip's own. Set them with `set_video`. A cutout's `edge`, `feather` and `background` do animate. |
151	| Any `shape` key | Shapes can't be animated, so `shape` isn't a group here. |
152	
153	### Animating graphic props
154	
155	A graphic clip's props are a fourth group: `graphic: {props: {<key>: <value>}}`, keyed by what its module declares. It mirrors the Graphic sub-tab's **Properties** with an action selected. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
156	
157	```json
158	{ "clip": 18, "action": 44, "patch": { "graphic": { "props": { "accent": "#ff5500", "count": 96 } } } }
159	```
160	
161	- A value is checked as `set_graphic` checks it, minimum and maximum included, against the module as the project's graphics folder holds it now.
162	- A number ramps along the curve and arrives with decimals, so 64 to 129 is 96.5 halfway. A module that needs a whole number rounds it.
163	- A colour blends in OKLab, with straight alpha.
164	- A string, a boolean and an enum switch to the end's value when the action ends.
165	- An image prop switches when the action ends. `""` names no image there.
166	- A prop the clip holds no value for starts from the module's current default, written into the clip in the same undo step.
167	- `graphic.props.<key>: null` removes that prop from the end, and `graphic: null` removes the whole group.
168	
169	`get_project` shows `kinds` beside `props`. Frame Job writes that and ignores any you send, so an end you read back can be sent again.
170	
171	**When it refuses.**
172	
173	- A prop its module marks `animate: false` is refused. Set it with `set_graphic`.
174	- `name`, `width`, `height`, `in` and `length` are refused: an action animates `graphic.props` only.
175	- While the module is missing or doesn't compile, a value is refused, and `get_graphic` says why. A `null` still removes.
176	- On a clip that isn't a graphic: "clip 7 is not a graphic clip".
177	
178	### Speed in an action
179	
180	`speed`, a number beside the groups, is a media clip's rate. The clip ramps from the rate in force to it along the curve and holds it after, and it keeps its start and length, playing more or less source. It mirrors the Speed section's **Rate** with an action selected. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/).
181	
182	```json
183	{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": { "speed": 3 } }
184	```
185	
186	The rate is clamped to ×0.1–×1000, and `speed: null` removes it.
187	
188	Above ×12 the clip's audio is left out, and the answer carries `audio_left_out` (the clip ids) and `audio_note`. Captions on a Captions track wholly inside a clip with sound are re-timed in the same step: `captions_retimed` lists them, and `captions_removed` lists those whose speech it no longer plays.
189	
190	**When it refuses.**
191	
192	- An end rate that would read past the end of the clip's media. The sentence names the largest end rate that fits.
193	- `speed: null` when the clip would then read past the end of its media. The sentence names the latest clip end that fits.
194	- A value that isn't a number or `null`, or a clip that isn't a media clip.
195	- A rate on a linked clip: "clip 7 is linked to clip 8: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction".
196	
197	### Switching off at an end
198	
199	`off` turns an optional property off at the end of the action. The path is stored as a `null` in the end state, where a `null` in `patch` removes the key instead. So `off` means "this shadow goes away by the end", and a `null` in `patch` means "stop animating the shadow".
200	
201	```json
202	{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": {}, "off": ["video.shadow", "audio.eq.band_2"] }
203	```
204	
205	- A path is `"group.key"`, with a group of `video`, `audio` or `text` and one of its top-level keys, such as `video.shadow`, `text.width` or `audio.limiter`.
206	- One deeper path exists: `audio.eq.<slot>` switches that EQ slot off. The slots are `high_pass`, `low_shelf`, `band_1`, `band_2`, `band_3`, `high_shelf` and `low_pass`.
207	- Only optional keys can go off. A required key such as `video.opacity` is refused.
208	- A path can't also be named in `patch`.
209	- `graphic` paths are refused: name the value a prop ends at in `patch`.
210	- `video.cutout` is refused: `set_video` with `{cutout: null}` removes a cutout.
211	- `video.motion`, `video.hide_silent` and `text.words` are refused here too.
212	
213	## `remove_action`
214	
215	Removes an action. The clip keeps its base properties. It mirrors the action lane's trash button and <kbd>⌫</kbd> with an action selected. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
216	
217	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
218	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
219	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
220	| `action` | integer | Yes | The action's id. |
221	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
222	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
223	
224	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. When the action named a speed, captions are re-timed in the same step, with `captions_retimed` and `captions_removed` as for `set_action`.
225	
226	**When it refuses.**
227	
228	- Removing a speed action when the clip would then read past the end of its media. The sentence names the latest clip end that fits.
229	- Removing a speed action from a linked clip: "clip 7 is linked to clip 8: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction".
230	- An action id the clip doesn't have is an error.

2	title: "Tools: transitions"
3	description: Make a transition at a hard cut from an agent, change its kind, length and easing, crossfade the sound, or remove it.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A [transition](/motion/transitions/) plays across the overlap between a clip and the clip before it on the same track, and it belongs to the later clip. Its length is that overlap. These tools make the overlap, choose the transition, and set how it eases and sounds.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  tools={['add_transition', 'set_transition', 'set_transition_duration', 'set_transition_style']}
12	  menu="Clip ▸ Transition ▸"
13	  where="Clip tab ▸ Transition section"
14	/>
15	
16	Start with `add_transition` at a hard cut. Use `set_transition` and `set_transition_duration` on clips that already overlap.
17	
18	Every time here is in ticks, 600,000 to the second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
19	
20	The kinds are `cross_dissolve`, `fade_black`, `fade_white`, `push_left`, `push_right`, `push_up`, `push_down`, `wipe`, `slide`, `zoom`, `wipe_left`, `wipe_up` and `wipe_down`. See [Transition styles](/motion/transition-styles/).
21	
22	An adjustment clip can't take a transition or overlap another clip, so these tools refuse one, and `set_transition` with `kind: null` is the only call that goes through. Fade it with opacity instead. See [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/).
23	
24	## `add_transition`
25	
26	Makes an overlap at the hard cut before a clip and puts a transition on it. It mirrors **Clip ▸ Transition ▸** on a clip that butts up against the one before it. See [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/).
27	
28	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
29	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
30	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The incoming clip's id. |
31	| `duration` | integer | Yes | The overlap you want. It can land shorter, but it's never refused for being too long. |
32	| `kind` | string | No | The transition. Left out, it's the clip's stored kind, else `cross_dissolve`. It can't be `null`: `set_transition` clears one. |
33	| `align` | string | No | Which side the overlap comes out of: `center`, the default, `before` or `after`. Ignored with `ripple`. |
34	| `ripple` | boolean or string | No | `true` makes the overlap by sliding the incoming clip and everything after it left, for two clips with no footage beyond the cut. The default is `false`. |
35	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
36	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
37	
38	```json
39	{ "clip": 15, "duration": 600000, "kind": "fade_black" }
40	```
41	
42	**How the overlap is made.** It's built from material the two clips already have: the source before the incoming clip's in point, and after the outgoing clip's out point. Nothing else on the timeline moves, and the pair's outer edges stay where they were.
43	
44	| `align` | Where the overlap comes from |
45	| --- | --- |
46	| `center` | Half from each side. An odd frame goes to the incoming clip, and a side with nothing to give passes its share to the other. |
47	| `before` | All from the incoming clip's head. |
48	| `after` | All from the outgoing clip's tail. |
49	
50	`duration` snaps down to whole frames. It's then held to each side's spare material, to the neighbours on the track and to the limit on how far two clips can overlap, so a request too long for the media lands shorter. A nest clip has no spare head, and its tail ends at the nest's own length.
51	
52	A stored transition keeps its curve and crossfade. A new one eases at both ends and crossfades its sound. The incoming clip's actions move with its new first frame, so a zoom stays on the source frame it was drawn over.
53	
54	**With `ripple: true`.** This is the sheet's **Shift Clips Left** button, for when neither clip has footage beyond the cut. No material is read and `align` is ignored. The incoming clip and every clip at or after the cut, on every unlocked track, slide left by `duration`, so the timeline gets that much shorter and no clip's source window changes.
55	
56	- The shift is capped at half the shorter of the two clips.
57	- It's also limited to the largest whole-frame shift that leaves every moved track within the overlap limit.
58	- A clip on another track pushed into its neighbour gets a `cross_dissolve`.
59	- Markers don't move.
60	
61	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary.
62	
63	**When it refuses.**
64	
65	- A `duration` that isn't positive is an error.
66	- A clip not at a hard cut is an error naming which of three: it's the first clip on its track, there's a gap before it, or it already overlaps a clip. For that last one, use `set_transition` or `set_transition_duration`.
67	- A `duration` under one frame is refused, naming the shortest that passes.
68	- A cut with no room: the request clamps to nothing against the two clips' spare material, their neighbours and the overlap limit. The sentence suggests `ripple: true`.
69	- A track already outside the overlap limit is refused by that rule before anything is fitted.
70	- With `ripple`: an incoming clip on a locked track, or clips with no room to overlap by shifting.
71	
72	## `set_transition`
73	
74	Sets the transition into a clip, or removes it. It mirrors the **Kind** pop-up in the Clip tab's **Transition** section. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
75	
76	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
77	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
78	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
79	| `kind` | string or null | Yes | The transition, or `null` to remove it. |
80	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
81	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
82	
83	The transition's length is the clip's overlap with the one before it, so a clip with no overlap ignores it until it has one. Make an overlap with `move_clip` or `set_transition_duration`. Changing the kind keeps the transition's curve and crossfade. A new one eases at both ends and crossfades its sound.
84	
85	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary.
86	
87	**When it refuses.** A missing `kind`, or a value that isn't one of the thirteen or `null`, is an error listing them.
88	
89	## `set_transition_duration`
90	
91	Makes a transition last `duration` by moving the clip, so its overlap with the clip before it equals that. It mirrors the **Duration** field in the Clip tab's **Transition** section. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
92	
93	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
94	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
95	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
96	| `duration` | integer | Yes | The overlap length, rounded to the frame grid. |
97	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
98	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
99	
100	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary.
101	
102	**When it refuses.**
103	
104	- On a track's first clip, which has nothing to overlap.
105	- Past half the shorter clip, snapped down. The sentence names that limit in ticks.
106	- A `duration` that isn't positive is an error. To clear a transition, use `set_transition` with `kind: null`.
107	
108	## `set_transition_style`
109	
110	Sets how a transition is eased, whether it crossfades the two clips' sound, and the crossfade's shape. It mirrors the **Curve** pop-up, the **Crossfade Audio** checkbox and the **Crossfade Shape** pop-up in the Clip tab's **Transition** section. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
111	
112	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
113	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
114	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
115	| `curve` | string | No | How the transition's progress is eased: `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` or `ease_in_out`. |
116	| `audio` | boolean or string | No | Crossfades the two clips' sound across the overlap. |
117	| `audio_shape` | string | No | The crossfade's curve. See the table below. |
118	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
119	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
120	
121	`audio` and `ripple` take `true` or `false`, or those words or `"1"` and `"0"` as strings.
122	
123	| `audio_shape` | The curve, over the eased progress p |
124	| --- | --- |
125	| `plus_3db` | The default, constant power: sine in, cosine out. It holds the level across two unrelated takes, where a straight-line pair dips 3 dB. |
126	| `linear` | p in, 1 − p out. |
127	| `s_curve` | A slow start. |
128	| `minus_3db` | A slow start. |
129	
130	The outgoing clip takes the shape of 1 − p.
131	
132	A key you leave out keeps what's there, so changing the curve never touches the crossfade, and the other way round.
133	
134	The tool writes onto any clip, with or without an overlap. A stored transition on a clip with no overlap isn't drawn until there is one. A clip with no transition at all gets a `cross_dissolve` with the style applied.
135	
136	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary.
137	
138	**When it refuses.** With none of the three keys, the call is an error naming them.
