Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_media.rs` — the media types (`Media`, `MediaOriginal`, `MediaKind`,
  spec §5.2's `media[]`), moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map
  "creator-jobs" CJ0b's toll T2) and re-exported by it, so every
  `crate::model::Media*` path holds; a media record's new keys land here.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s
  `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence (`audio.eq.<slot>.frequency
  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not
  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stage is Swift's.
- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /
  `check_de_esser` / `check_leveller`, run by
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence
  (`audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21`; times through
  `props_check.rs`'s `ticks_in_range`), `check_compressor` /
  `check_limiter` (under a prefix: `audio.` for the clip's, run by
  `check_audio`, and the track's own key for `track_dynamics.rs`, spec §11
  AU-150), and `clamp_gate` / `clamp_de_esser` / `clamp_leveller`
  (each field to its range, NaN to its default), run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stages are Swift's.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s

Keys: x, y (canvas px from the canvas centre, y DOWN), scale (1 = native pixels, 0.01–10), rotation (degrees, positive turns clockwise on screen), opacity (0–1), crop ({l, t, r, b} in SOURCE px — cropping never shifts the content), corner_radius (source px), shadow (null or {color, opacity, blur, angle, distance}), color ({brightness, contrast, saturation, hue, exposure, temperature, tint, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, vibrance, fade}, each 0 = unchanged and any subset merging — exposure is -3 to 3 (EV), fade 0–1 and the other seven tone keys -1 to 1, refused outside; a positive temperature is warmer, a positive tint more magenta; hue is in degrees, and a positive hue turns every colour's HSV hue that far, red → yellow → green, keeping its Rec. 709 luma), chroma (null or {key: [r, g, b], tolerance, softness, spill}), filters (an ARRAY of {kind, amount} applied in order, at most 4 — kind is blur|sharpen|pixelate|sepia|noir|vignette|invert and amount is 0–1; send the whole array, since it replaces rather than merges, and [] clears the stack), reflection (null or {opacity, height, gap, falloff} — height and falloff are fractions of the layer's cropped height, gap is source px), spotlight (null or {shape: rect|ellipse, x, y, width, height, feather, dim, zoom} — the centre and the box are SOURCE px from the cropped rect's centre, dim is how much darker it is OUTSIDE and zoom 1–2 magnifies what is inside), obscure (an ARRAY of {shape: rect|ellipse, x, y, width, height, feather, kind, amount} that HIDES what is under each one, at most 4 — kind is blur|pixelate and amount is 0–1, feather is the source px the effect ramps in over, and the centre and the box are SOURCE px from the cropped rect's centre, the same frame the spotlight uses. Like filters it is replaced whole rather than merged, so send the whole array and [] to clear it), blend (how this layer combines with what is already on the canvas: normal|multiply|screen|add|overlay|darken|lighten|difference — normal is source-over, which is what every project drew before this key existed. A blend needs something UNDER it: over the empty canvas multiply, darken and overlay read black while screen, add, lighten and difference change nothing, so add_background is usually the call before this one. It is forced to normal for the length of a cross dissolve, whose own weighting requires it, so what the frame shows there can legitimately differ from the value get_project reports), motion (what the clip DOES: null, or {in, out, during} — in and out are {kind: fade|zoom_in|zoom_out|slide_left|slide_right|slide_up|slide_down|spin|pop, duration: ticks} measured from the clip's first and last frame, during is {kind: pulse|shake|spin|bounce|drift, amount: 0–1, period: ticks} over the whole clip and drift ignores its period. Like every other object here it MERGES: a slot you leave out keeps what is stored, a slot set to null clears that slot, {motion: null} clears the whole preset, and a motion with no slot left reads back as null. The two durations are snapped to the document's frame grid and the period is snapped with a floor of ONE frame (it divides in every during formula and has no zero), so get_project can answer with a tick count near the one you sent rather than the one itself. in + out longer than the clip scales both down to meet rather than refusing. It is NOT an animation target — set_action_end refuses it — and get_project reports the clip UN-MOVED, since the preset becomes placement only when a frame is rendered), wheels ({lift, gamma, gain}, each {x, y, master}, each -1 to 1 and 0 = unchanged: x, y is the colour push, its angle the hue (0° red, 120° green, 240° blue) and its length the strength, and must lie inside the unit circle (x² + y² ≤ 1); master is the brightness; refused outside, never clamped. //! Reading a caller-authored patch: the walk, the merge and the typed read
//! that every property patch in the crate comes through.
//!
//! A **patch** is a partial property object an op merges into a clip's
//! property group (`CONTEXT.md`). It merges key by key at every depth, an
//! array replaces its list, and `null` clears an optional key. It is the one
//! thing in the schema a CALLER writes rather than this crate — a typed
//! Swift builder, an MCP call, a project written by hand — so it is the one
//! thing that has to be read suspiciously. The rule the whole file exists
//! for: **a key or a value the vocabulary does not have is refused, never
//! dropped and never corrected** — [`check_keys`] walks a patch's keys and
//! JSON kinds against the group's own template, [`merge_group`] merges and
//! reads the result back as its type, and [`check_group_patch`] does both

//! `edit_action.rs` builds an action's end-patch door out of. Every refusal

72	            Group::Audio => "an audio patch",
73	            Group::Text => "a text patch",
74	            Group::Shape => "a shape patch",
75	        }
76	    }

201	/// Rejects any key in `patch` the group's schema does not have, and any
202	/// value whose JSON kind is not the one the schema has there, naming the
203	/// dotted path to it — array indices included, so `filters[1].kindd` says
204	/// WHICH entry to fix, where a bare `filters.kindd` would leave the caller
205	/// comparing every entry it sent. `path` is the path to `patch` itself,
206	/// empty at the group's root. Recursion is bounded by the same depth action
207	/// patches use; past it the check stops rather than walking an arbitrary
208	/// tree, and serde drops whatever it finds there.
209	fn check_keys(
210	    patch: &Value,
211	    template: &Value,
212	    subject: &str,
213	    path: &str,
214	    depth: u32,
215	) -> Result<(), String> {
216	    // The kind comes first, and it is not only a nicer sentence than
217	    // serde's `expected struct Duck`: serde READS two wrong kinds. A struct
218	    // deserializes from a JSON array of its fields in declaration order, so
219	    // `{"duck": [0.9, 300000, 600000]}` would store a duck, and a unit
220	    // variant from a one-key object, so `{"blend": {"multiply": null}}`
221	    // would store a blend — spellings the caller never learnt from
222	    // `get_project` and a typo could land on by accident.
223	    if let Some(expected) = wrong_kind(patch, template) {
224	        return Err(format!(
225	            "bad value at \"{path}\" in {subject}: expected {expected}, not {}",
226	            describe(patch)
227	        ));
228	    }
229	    // An array of objects — `video.filters`, and from format version 4
230	    // `video.obscure` — is where the schema puts keys inside an array, and
231	    // every element has the SAME shape, so the template's first entry
232	    // describes all of them. Without this a misspelled
233	    // `{"filters": [{"amont": 1}]}` would be dropped in silence by serde,
234	    // the failure this check exists to prevent. Arrays of numbers (a
235	    // colour, `from`/`to`) fall through harmlessly: a number against a
236	    // number has no keys to check.
237	    if let (Value::Array(given), Value::Array(known)) = (patch, template) {
238	        if depth < MAX_PATCH_DEPTH {
239	            if let Some(reference) = known.first() {
240	                let required = COMPLETE_ENTRIES
241	                    .iter()
242	                    .find(|(key, _)| *key == last_segment(path))
243	                    .map(|(_, keys)| *keys);
244	                for (index, value) in given.iter().enumerate() {
245	                    let here = format!("{path}[{index}]");
246	                    check_keys(value, reference, subject, &here, depth + 1)?;
247	                    if let Some(required) = required {
248	                        check_complete(value, required, subject, &here)?;
249	                    }
250	                }
251	            }
252	        }
253	        return Ok(());
254	    }
255	    let (Value::Object(given), Value::Object(known)) = (patch, template) else {
256	        // A leaf or a `null` (clearing an optional group): no keys to
257	        // check.
258	        return Ok(());
259	    };
260	    if depth >= MAX_PATCH_DEPTH {
261	        return Ok(());
262	    }
263	    for (key, value) in given {
264	        let here = if path.is_empty() {
265	            key.clone()
266	        } else {
267	            format!("{path}.{key}")
268	        };
269	        let Some(reference) = known.get(key) else {
270	            return Err(format!("unknown key \"{here}\" in {subject}"));
271	        };
272	        check_keys(value, reference, subject, &here, depth + 1)?;
273	    }
274	    Ok(())
275	}
276	
277	/// The lists whose entries a patch must spell out IN FULL, by the key that
278	/// holds them.
279	///
280	/// An array replaces its list (`CONTEXT.md`), so an entry in a patch is
281	/// merged over NOTHING and every key it leaves out comes from the type's
282	/// serde defaults instead. For `video.filters` that completion is a picture
283	/// nobody asked for: `{"filters": [{"amount": 1}]}` reads as "the same
284	/// filter, more of it", which is what it means while an action interpolates
285	/// it, and lands as a half-strength BLUR — the two keys ARE the filter, and
286	/// neither has a defensible default when the other is named.
287	///
288	/// The schema's other two lists of objects are deliberately NOT here:
289	/// `video.obscure` is a box whose six geometry defaults are a real, centred
290	/// region and `shape.gradient.stops` is a position and a colour, so in both
291	/// an omitted key leaves the entry recognisably the thing the caller named.
292	/// The match is on the LAST segment of the path, so the rule holds at
293	/// `filters` in a group patch and at `video.filters` in an end patch
294	/// without being written twice.
295	///
296	/// The required keys are SPELLED rather than taken from the template's own
297	/// entry, and the difference only shows up later: a field added to
298	/// [`crate::model::Filter`] would otherwise join the requirement the day it
299	/// landed and refuse every patch every agent had already learnt to write —
300	/// where a new field's serde default is, by construction, the value every
301	/// older project already has.
302	///
303	/// `text.words` (format version 9) is the second entry, for the filter's
304	/// reason read on a clock: a word IS its two times, and a `{"start": …}`
305	/// whose `end` came from the type's default would be a word that ends at
306	/// clip time 0 — before it starts, which `check_text` would then refuse in
307	/// a sentence about an `end` the caller never sent. Naming the missing key
308	/// is the refusal that tells the caller what to fix.
309	const COMPLETE_ENTRIES: [(&str, &[&str]); 2] = [
310	    ("filters", &["kind", "amount"]),
311	    ("words", &["start", "end"]),
312	];
313	
314	/// The last dotted segment of `path` — the key an array is held under,
315	/// which is what [`COMPLETE_ENTRIES`] is matched against.
316	fn last_segment(path: &str) -> &str {
317	    path.rsplit('.').next().unwrap_or(path)
318	}
319	
320	/// Refuses an entry of a [`COMPLETE_ENTRIES`] list that does not name every
321	/// `required` key, by the path to the key it left out. A `null` is not a
322	/// spelling of a key either: it clears an optional field, and nothing named
323	/// here is optional.
324	fn check_complete(
325	    entry: &Value,
326	    required: &[&str],
327	    subject: &str,
328	    path: &str,
329	) -> Result<(), String> {
330	    let Value::Object(given) = entry else {
331	        return Ok(());
332	    };
333	    for key in required {
334	        if given.get(*key).unwrap_or(&Value::Null).is_null() {
335	            return Err(format!("missing key \"{path}.{key}\" in {subject}"));
336	        }
337	    }
338	    Ok(())
339	}
340	
341	/// Reads a merged group back as its type, naming the path and the value of
342	/// whatever only the TYPE can refuse — a misspelt variant, a `null` a
343	/// required field cannot take, a colour of the wrong length.
344	///
345	/// `serde_path_to_error` is what makes the path possible: serde's sentence
346	/// names the value and what the vocabulary allows, but not which of four
347	/// filters it was in. `prefix` is what the path hangs off when the group is
348	/// not the root — its name inside an end patch — so one sentence serves
349	/// both doors.
350	fn read_merged<T: DeserializeOwned>(
351	    merged: Value,
352	    subject: &str,
353	    prefix: &str,
354	) -> Result<T, String> {
355	    serde_path_to_error::deserialize(merged).map_err(|e| {
356	        let path = path_under(prefix, &e.path().to_string());
357	        format!("bad value at \"{path}\" in {subject}: {}", e.inner())
358	    })
359	}
360	
361	/// Where a `serde_path_to_error` path sits under `prefix` — the one
362	/// spelling of that join, because there are two callers and the trap is
363	/// invisible from either: `Path`'s ROOT prints as `"."` and not as the
364	/// empty string, so the naive `format!("{prefix}.{inside}")` reads
365	/// `video..` for an error at the group itself. Both spellings of "the whole
366	/// thing" collapse onto `prefix` here.
367	///
368	/// `edit_zoom.rs`'s `ZoomRegion` is the second caller, and it is what found
369	/// this: its `region..` was reachable from the app the moment D1·5 stopped
370	/// the Swift side refusing a missing member first.
371	pub(crate) fn path_under(prefix: &str, inside: &str) -> String {
372	    let inside = if inside == "." { "" } else { inside };
373	    match (prefix, inside) {
374	        ("", inside) => inside.to_string(),
375	        (prefix, "") => prefix.to_string(),
376	        (prefix, inside) => format!("{prefix}.{inside}"),
377	    }
378	}
379	
380	/// The refusal every walk gives for a key the vocabulary does not have,
381	/// spelled once so a door that walks a patch group by group
382	/// (`edit_action.rs`'s end patch) says it in the same words.
383	pub(crate) fn unknown_key(path: &str, subject: &str) -> String {
384	    format!("unknown key \"{path}\" in {subject}")
385	}
386	
387	/// Walks and reads ONE group's body out of a patch that is not being merged
388	/// into a stored group — an action's end state, where the patch is a patch
389	/// of a patch and there is no clip to merge into.
390	///
391	/// `prefix` is where the body sits in the patch (`video`), so the paths the
392	/// refusals name carry it: `bad value at "video.filters[1].kind"`. The read
393	/// goes against the group's own TEMPLATE, which is what lets a sparse patch
394	/// read at all; the merged value is thrown away, because only the refusal
395	/// is wanted. It is a walk and a read and NOT a range check: the state a
396	/// clip interpolates toward may legitimately name a value no stored group
397	/// could hold, and `actions_clamp.rs`'s `clamp_video` bounds the evaluated value
398	/// instead.
399	///
400	/// **A `null` here can only be a REMOVAL**, there being no stored value to
401	/// clear, so the read never sees one: `{"crop": null}` is "stop animating
402	/// the crop", where the same spelling in a `set_video` patch is a required
403	/// field being cleared and is refused. The WALK does see it, which is what
404	/// keeps `{"blurr": null}` an unknown key rather than a key quietly
405	/// dropped.
406	pub(crate) fn check_group_patch(
407	    body: &Value,
408	    group: Group,
409	    subject: &str,
410	    prefix: &str,
411	) -> Result<(), String> {
412	    let template = group.template();

423	/// A copy of `patch` with every `null`-valued key dropped, at every depth —
424	/// [`check_group_patch`]'s removal rule, and the shape `edit_action.rs`'s
425	/// `prune_removed` applies to the STORED end state. Only object keys go: a
426	/// `null` inside a list is not a removal, and the read refuses it by index.
427	fn without_nulls(patch: &Value, depth: u32) -> Value {
428	    let Value::Object(fields) = patch else {
429	        return patch.clone();
430	    };
431	    if depth >= MAX_PATCH_DEPTH {
432	        return patch.clone();
433	    }
434	    Value::Object(
435	        fields
436	            .iter()
437	            .filter(|(_, value)| !value.is_null())
438	            .map(|(key, value)| (key.clone(), without_nulls(value, depth + 1)))
439	            .collect(),
440	    )
441	}

443	/// The JSON kind the schema has where the template holds `reference`, as a
444	/// refusal says it, when `given` is NOT that kind; `None` when it is.
445	///
446	/// A `null` on either side passes: in a patch it clears, and whether the
447	/// field may be cleared is the read's to say (an optional takes it, a
448	/// required one refuses it). A number is one kind with one refinement —
449	/// the template writes every `f64` with a fraction and every tick count
450	/// without one, so a fraction where a tick count belongs is named here
451	/// rather than as serde's `expected i64`.
452	fn wrong_kind(given: &Value, reference: &Value) -> Option<&'static str> {
453	    let fits = match (given, reference) {
454	        (Value::Null, _) | (_, Value::Null) => true,
455	        (Value::Number(given), Value::Number(reference)) => reference.is_f64() || !given.is_f64(),
456	        (Value::Bool(_), Value::Bool(_))
457	        | (Value::String(_), Value::String(_))
458	        | (Value::Array(_), Value::Array(_))
459	        | (Value::Object(_), Value::Object(_)) => true,
460	        _ => false,
461	    };
462	    if fits {
463	        return None;
464	    }
465	    Some(match reference {
466	        Value::Number(number) if !number.is_f64() => "a whole number",
467	        Value::Number(_) => "a number",
468	        Value::Bool(_) => "true or false",
469	        Value::String(_) => "a string",
470	        Value::Array(_) => "a list",
471	        Value::Object(_) | Value::Null => "an object",
472	    })
473	}

475	/// Checks the patch's keys and kinds, merges it into `base` and reads the
476	/// merged group back as its type — the one door every caller-authored patch
477	/// of a group comes through, `set_*` and the `text` / `shape` of a new clip
478	/// alike. The merge itself is `actions::merge`, the one deep merge in the
479	/// crate.
480	///
481	/// The walk has already refused an unknown key and a value of the wrong
482	/// kind; the read ([`read_merged`]) is where what only the TYPE knows is
483	/// caught — a misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take, a
484	/// colour of the wrong length. The path it names is into the MERGED group,
485	/// which is the patch's path too: the merge keeps every key where the patch
486	/// put it and an array replaces whole, and the base was written by this
487	/// crate and reads back cleanly, so the only values that can fail are the
488	/// patch's.
489	pub(crate) fn merge_group<T: Serialize + DeserializeOwned>(
490	    base: &T,
491	    patch: &Value,
492	    group: Group,
493	) -> Result<T, String> {
494	    if !patch.is_object() {
495	        return Err(format!(
496	            "{} patch must be a json object, not {}",
497	            group.name(),
498	            describe(patch)
499	        ));
500	    }
501	    check_keys(patch, &group.template(), group.subject(), "", 0)?;
502	    let merged = actions::merge(&actions::to_json(base), patch);
503	    read_merged(merged, group.subject(), "")
504	}
505	//! Adjustment clips (spec §11 GR-6): a clip kind with no picture of its
506	//! own. While it lasts, its `video.color` (all thirteen keys), its wheels
507	//! (spec §11 GR-11), its curves (GR-12), its look, its point filters (sepia, noir, vignette,
508	//! invert) and its opacity — the STRENGTH —
509	//! apply to everything already drawn behind it in its container (to the
510	//! pixels its qualifier selects, GR-13), the canvas
511	//! background included, and never to a track in front. The compositor's
512	//! eighth pipeline does the grading by reading the target it draws into
513	//! (`Compositor+Adjustment.swift`); the core's part is the kind, the op,
514	//! the rules below and the recipe's `{"kind":"adjustment"}` source.
515	//!
516	//! What it refuses, and why each is a refusal rather than a clamp:
517	//!
518	//! - **A nest.** A nest is flattened into the clips inside it, and an
519	//!   adjustment clip in there would grade the PARENT's layers behind the
520	//!   nest clip as well as the nest's own, which is not what a nest means.
521	//!   `nest` refuses it ([`adjustment_cannot_nest`]); `validate` errors on one
522	//!   inside a nest ([`adjustment_nested`]), which is what a file and a paste
523	//!   into a scope meet, because a scoped edit is validated on the MERGED
524	//!   parent (`scope.rs`); and `add_adjustment_clip` has no meaning inside a
525	//!   scope (`scope.rs`'s `refused_inside`).
526	//! - **A transition.** Both halves of a dissolve are drawn into one
527	//!   destination as a weighted pair; a pass that grades the destination has
528	//!   no half to be. `add_transition`, `set_transition` and
529	//!   `set_transition_style` refuse ([`adjustment_transition`]), and so does
530	//!   the overlap rule for any pair that holds one
531	//!   ([`adjustment_overlap`], called from `transition.rs`'s
532	//!   `check_overlap_rule`, the one placement door) — so
533	//!   `set_gained_transitions` never mints a transition on one. Fade it with
534	//!   opacity instead.
535	//! - **Blur, sharpen, pixelate and a blend mode.** The neighbourhood
536	//!   filters sample the layer's own texture around a pixel, and there is
537	//!   none; a blend combines a layer's colour with the canvas, and an
538	//!   adjustment clip has no colour of its own. `set_video`, `paste` and
539	//!   `paste_attributes` meet [`check_adjustment_video`] beside `check_blend`
540	//!   (errors, its precedent), and an action's end carrying one is closed by
541	//!   the evaluator ([`clamp_adjustment`]), as `clamp_video` closes a nest's
542	//!   blend.
543	//!
544	//! **On a matte track it is inert** ([`Project::inert_adjustment`]): a
545	//! matte group is one track, and two clips on one track share an instant
546	//! only in a transition, which is refused, so the clip could only be the
547	//! group's sole member and would act as an EMPTY matte. The recipe leaves
548	//! it out before the mattes are answered. On a track CUT by a matte it
549	//! grades only inside the matte, which needs nothing here: the compositor
550	//! weights its pass by the coverage like any matted layer's.
551	//!
552	//! Its stored transform, crop, corner, shadow, reflection, chroma,
553	//! spotlight, obscure and motion placement are kept and do nothing;
554	//! refusing them would make Paste Attributes fail from any moved clip.
555	//!
556	//! **The qualifier is its alone** (spec §11 GR-13): `video.qualifier`
557	//! narrows which of the destination's pixels the pass grades, read before
558	//! the grade. On any other clip a non-neutral one is an error in its own
559	//! sentence ([`check_qualifier_clip`], beside `check_adjustment_video` in
560	//! `set_video`, `paste` and `paste_attributes`); one reached through a file
561	//! or an action's end on another clip is inert, because the recipe
562	//! publishes it only in an adjustment source (`recipe.rs`'s
563	//! `layer_source`). Paste Attributes drops it onto a picture clip, and an
564	//! adjustment target keeps its own when the payload clip is not an
565	//! adjustment clip (`edit_paste_attributes.rs`'s `copy_group`).

568	use crate::model::{BlendMode, Clip, FilterKind, Project, Source, VideoProps};

573	impl Project {
574	    /// An adjustment clip at `at` on `track`, five seconds long unless
575	    /// `duration` says otherwise, at scale 1 with default `video` (spec §6,
576	    /// §11 GR-6). Placed through `add_described_clip`, so the overlap rule
577	    /// and its sentence are the same as any sourceless clip's — with the
578	    /// adjustment clause, since no overlap may hold one.
579	    pub fn add_adjustment_clip(
580	        &self,
581	        track: u32,
582	        at: Ticks,
583	        duration: Option<Ticks>,
584	    ) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
585	        self.add_described_clip(

605	            && !instance.track.matte.is_none()

609	/// Whether the clip is an adjustment clip.

611	    matches!(clip.source, Source::Adjustment)

614	/// The one rule about an adjustment CLIP's video group: no neighbourhood
615	/// filter and no blend mode. An `Err`, as `check_blend`'s is, so `paste` and
616	/// `paste_attributes` meet it through `settle_video` and refuse the whole
617	/// paste. Any other clip passes.
618	pub(crate) fn check_adjustment_video(clip: &Clip, props: &VideoProps) -> Result<(), String> {
619	    if !is_adjustment(clip) {
620	        return Ok(());
621	    }
622	    for filter in &props.filters {
623	        let name = match filter.kind {
624	            FilterKind::Blur => "blur",
625	            FilterKind::Sharpen => "sharpen",
626	            FilterKind::Pixelate => "pixelate",
627	            FilterKind::Sepia | FilterKind::Noir | FilterKind::Vignette | FilterKind::Invert => {
628	                continue
629	            }
630	        };
631	        return Err(format!(
632	            "clip {} is an adjustment clip and cannot take the {name} filter",
633	            clip.id
634	        ));
635	    }
636	    if props.blend != BlendMode::Normal {
637	        return Err(format!(
638	            "clip {} is an adjustment clip and cannot take a blend mode",
639	            clip.id
640	        ));
641	    }
642	    Ok(())
643	}

648	/// [`check_adjustment_video`]'s), so `paste` and `paste_attributes` meet it
649	/// through `settle_video`.
650	pub(crate) fn check_qualifier_clip(clip: &Clip, props: &VideoProps) -> Result<(), String> {
651	    if is_adjustment(clip) || props.qualifier.is_neutral() {
652	        return Ok(());
653	    }
654	    Err(format!(
655	        "clip {} is not an adjustment clip and cannot take a qualifier",
656	        clip.id
657	    ))

666	        b
667	    } else if is_adjustment(a) {
668	        a
669	    } else {

671	    };
672	    Some(format!(
673	        "clips {} and {} would overlap, and clip {} is an adjustment clip, which cannot take a \

677	}

681	pub(crate) fn adjustment_transition(clip: &Clip) -> Option<String> {

693	pub(crate) fn adjustment_nested(clip: u32, whose: &str) -> String {

697	}

699	/// `nest`'s refusal for a selection holding an adjustment clip.
700	pub(crate) fn adjustment_cannot_nest(clip: u32) -> String {
701	    format!("clip {clip} is an adjustment clip, and an adjustment clip cannot go inside a nest")

705	/// action's end is checked against the vocabulary, never the clip): a

707	pub(crate) fn clamp_adjustment(mut props: VideoProps) -> VideoProps {

import Foundation

/// The catalog row of `analyze_cutout` (spec §11 CO-31; road map "creator-jobs" CO3), spliced
/// in by `creatorTools()`.
extension AgentServer {

    func cutoutTools() -> [[String: Any]] {
        [
            // It mirrors the Clip tab's Picture ▸ Background section — its Status read-out and
            // its Analyze Now button (VideoPane+Cutout.swift, EditorViewController+Cutout.swift's
            // analyzeCutoutNow) — whose checkbox and Clip ▸ Remove Background are `set_video`'s
            // `cutout`. An app-state read that makes masks: no op, no `scope`, no undo step.
            tool(
                "analyze_cutout",
                "Answers where Remove Background stands for cut-out clips (a clip whose "
                    + "set_video cutout is set) and makes their masks now — the mirror of the "
                    + "Clip tab's Picture ▸ Background section's Status and its Analyze Now "
                    + "button; Clip ▸ Remove Background and the section's checkbox turn a "
                    + "cutout on (set_video {cutout: {}}). The masks are made ON THIS MAC "
                    + "(Vision's person segmentation, or for a picture with subject foreground "
                    + "its foreground instance mask) — no upload, no network request, no API "
                    + "key — and kept per media in the project's cache, so frames already "
                    + "analysed are never analysed again. A picture (an image clip) is one "
                    + "frame, made from the picture itself. A call wants every frame the clips "
                    + "play and runs again an analysis that failed or was stopped, then waits "
                    + "up to wait seconds (0 when left out: the status now, at most 60) for "
                    + "every clip to settle; it never refuses for time — call again to keep "
                    + "waiting. Answers clips [{clip, media, state, progress, quality, frames, "
                    + "covered, ready, subject_found, centroid, error?}]: state is analyzing, "
                    + "ready (every frame analysed and a person, or a picture's foreground "
                    + "subject, found), no_person (every frame analysed and no person in the "
                    + "clip's window: the clip draws whole), no_subject (a picture with subject "
                    + "foreground whose mask found no subject: it draws whole), failed or "
                    + "no_picture (the clip plays no frame of its file); progress 0–1; quality "

Other edits do the same; see [Overlaps make transitions](#overlaps-make-transitions). docs/guide/editing.md:287:- **The overlap rule.** On one track, a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half the length of the shorter clip. Moves, trims, nudges, duplicates, gap closes and nests that would break it are refused. Paste and Un-nest put such clips on a new front track instead. Ripple deletes are never refused by it: a clip a ripple slides onto a neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve (below). docs/guide/editing.md:288:- **Overlaps make transitions.** Any edit that leaves a clip overlapping the clip before it on its track gives it a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition: moves, trims, duplicates, pastes, ripple deletes, Close Gap, Nest and Un-nest. content.content:
### Filters

A clip can carry up to **four** filters. They are applied in list order, so
blur-then-sepia looks different from sepia-then-blur.

- **Add Filter** appends a Blur at 50 %.
- Each filter's row starts with a number popup that is its place in the
  stack. Pick a different number to move the filter.
Limits:

- A cross dissolve draws as Normal for as long as the clips overlap.
- The Blend popup is greyed on a nest clip, because a nest has no pixels of its
  own to blend. Un-nest it (⇧⌘G) to blend the clips inside.
docs/site/src/content/docs/canvas/blend-modes.mdx:25:Every clip starts on **Normal**. The change is one undo step, and with several clips selected it applies to all of them.
docs/site/src/content/docs/canvas/blend-modes.mdx:31:These are in the popup's order. "Underneath" means every layer behind this one, and the canvas background.
docs/site/src/content/docs/canvas/blend-modes.mdx:35:| **Normal** | Draws over what's underneath. |
docs/site/src/content/docs/canvas/blend-modes.mdx:66:A layer always draws as **Normal** for as long as it's in a [transition](/motion/transitions/), whatever blend mode it has. The popup keeps showing the clip's own mode during the overlap. Only the frames in the overlap draw as Normal.
docs/site/src/content/docs/canvas/blend-modes.mdx:82:`set_video` sets the mode with `blend`, one of `normal`, `multiply`, `screen`, `add`, `overlay`, `darken`, `lighten` or `difference`. Any mode but `normal` on a nest clip gets the error "clip 7 shows a nest and cannot take a blend mode". See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#transform-position-scale-rotation-opacity-and-blend).
docs/site/src/content/docs/effects/filters.mdx:52:## Stack and reorder filters
docs/site/src/content/docs/effects/filters.mdx:56:The place doesn't decide everything, because Frame Job always works through a stack in this order:
docs/site/src/content/docs/effects/filters.mdx:62:5. Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert, in the order of their places.
docs/site/src/content/docs/effects/filters.mdx:64:So the order only changes the picture among Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert. Noir then Sepia gives a warm black and white, while Sepia then Noir gives a plain one. Moving a Blur above or below a Sepia changes nothing.

fixed.was: `filters` are "applied in order, so blur then sepia differs from sepia then blur"
fixed.now: Sepia, noir, vignette and invert run in list order. Blur, sharpen and pixelate always run before them, wherever they sit in the list.

fixed.was: "A left-out `kind` is `blur` and a left-out `amount` is 0.5."
fixed.now: Each entry must name both keys: leaving one out is an error.

fixed.was: "The grade runs in this order: color, wheels, curves, look, then filters."
fixed.now: Ends with "then the sepia, noir, vignette and invert filters", because the blur, sharpen and pixelate filters run earlier.

fixed.was: A blend is forced to `normal` for the length of a cross dissolve
fixed.now: Forced to `normal` for the length of any transition, and on a clip on a matte track

fixed.was: Over the empty canvas, multiply, darken and overlay read black
fixed.now: Over an empty black canvas, because the canvas background can be another colour

fixed.was: The chroma key's colour is the one exception to four-number colours
fixed.now: Two keys differ: the chroma key is three numbers, and the cursor's `click_color` is a CSS colour

fixed.was: behind_subject is cut by cut-out clips on a track behind it in the same container
fixed.now: Adds "or inside a nest on such a track"

fixed.was: `hue` keeps "its Rec. 709 brightness"
fixed.now: Keeps "its brightness", because the luma weights are BT.2020's in an HLG project

fixed.was: Qualifier: "A colour with a chroma under about 0.06 has no hue and is never selected by it."
fixed.now: A colour's selection fades out as its chroma falls from 0.06 to 0.02, and at 0.02 or under it's never selected.

fixed.was: Qualifier luma: "Rec. 709 luma."
fixed.now: Rec. 709 luma, or BT.2020 luma in an HLG project.

fixed.was: An unnamed clip shows "the nest, the media file, or its kind"
fixed.now: Adds "a text clip's words"

fixed.was: text_behind_subject's candidate and refusal rules left out that a clip's video must be on
fixed.now: Candidates, the no-clip refusal and the named-clip refusal all say "with its video on" ("with their video on" for the candidates)

fixed.was: "Above ×12 the clip's audio is left out, and the answer carries audio_left_out"
fixed.now: The call that takes the clip above ×12 answers with `audio_left_out` and `audio_note`. A clip already above is not reported again.

fixed.was: An end rate that reads past the media's end: the sentence names the largest end rate that fits
fixed.now: Adds: or, when none down to ×0.1 does, the latest clip end that fits at ×0.1

fixed.was: add_transition: "`duration` snaps down to whole frames."
fixed.now: `duration` rounds to the nearest frame.

fixed.was: "A `duration` that isn't positive is an error."
fixed.now: A `duration` that isn't positive once it's rounded to the frame grid is an error.

fixed.was: `s_curve` and `minus_3db` were both "A slow start."
fixed.now: `s_curve`: a slow start and a slow finish. `minus_3db`: a slow start, rising fastest at the end.

removed: mcp/tools-transitions: the refusal bullet "A `duration` under one frame is refused, naming the shortest that passes." The tool rounds `duration` to the frame grid before the core sees it, so a request under half a frame becomes 0 and gets the not-positive error, and anything else is at least one frame (app/Sources/AgentServer+Arguments.swift:418-428).
guide_errors: docs/guide/canvas-and-layers.md:487-488: "They are applied in list order, so blur-then-sepia looks different from sepia-then-blur." This is false. Only sepia, noir, vignette and invert run in list order (Compositor.metal:1573, 1629-1633). docs/guide/color-grading.md:34 already has it right.
docs/guide/canvas-and-layers.md:231: "A cross dissolve draws as Normal for as long as the clips overlap." Any transition does, and so does a clip on a matte track (core/src/recipe.rs:311-315).
